subject: another question about using inbred lines

messages.author: b36e760cb8e51ce1
messages.subject: another question about using inbred lines
parts:
Hi,
Sorry to return to the problem of mapping with recombinant inbred
lines, but I am having trouble. Using class(myx)[1] <- "riself" does
not seem to get me the expected change in map length:

> test<-read.cross("csv",,"simple_test.csv",genotypes=c("A","B"))
--Read the following data:
100 individuals
3 markers
1 phenotypes
> summary(test)
Backcross

No. individuals: 100

No. phenotypes: 1
Percent phenotyped: 100

No. chromosomes: 1
Autosomes: 1

Total markers: 3
No. markers: 3
Percent genotyped: 100
Genotypes (%): AA:40 AB:60
> pull.map(test)
M1 M2 M3
0.0 10.10135 20.20270
> est.map(test)
M1 M2 M3
0.00000 11.14730 22.29460
attr(,"loglik")
[1] -134.3392
> class(test)[1] <- "riself"
> summary(test)
RI strains via selfing

No. individuals: 100

No. phenotypes: 1
Percent phenotyped: 100

No. chromosomes: 1
Autosomes: 1

Total markers: 3
No. markers: 3
Percent genotyped: 100
Genotypes (%): AA:40 BB:60
> pull.map(test)
M1 M2 M3
0.00000 10.10135 20.20270
> est.map(test)
M1 M2 M3
0.000000 5.883665 11.767329
attr(,"loglik")
[1] -134.3392
>

What am I doing wrong? It seems that the change in population type is
recognised, but has no immediate effect on the map length. The
existing map is therefore used in QTL mapping. I suppose I could
replace the existing map with the expanded map estimated within R/QTL,
but that isn't the same thing as expanding the given map. Would a
suitable alternative be to expand the map outside R/QTL using r = 2R/
(1=2R), use this in the input file and then treat the population as a
backcross.

Thanks
Ian

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] another question about using inbred lines
parts:
Dear Ian,

Whether the cross is treated as a backcross ("bc") or RIL by selfing
("riself"),
in the est.map function, we seek to estimate recombination fractions
between markers
(using a multipoint algorithm). If the cross type is "riself", these
recombination
fractions are then contracted using r' = (r/2) / (1-r). Then in
either case these
are converted to genetic distances using a map function (by default,
the Haldane
map function is used).

In the calculation of QTL genotype probabilities (given the marker
data) for
use in interval mapping, the genetic distances get converted back to
recombination
fractions using a map function, and, for the cross type "riself",
these recombination
fractions are expanded using R = (2r)/(1+2r).

If you use the map estimated from the data (via est.map), the QTL
mapping results will
be the same, whether you'd used cross type "bc" or "riself". The
only difference is that,
with cross type "riself" the map will be approximately that
corresponding to meiosis,
while if you used cross type "bc" the map would be expanded by about 2x.

You can see that in your results below. est.map delivers a map that
is 22 cM long
when you have cross type "bc", and one that is 12 cM long when you
use cross type "riself".

Changing the cross type doesn't change the internal map within the
object. You need to
use est.map and then replace.map to do that, and you'd want to run
those after you change
the cross type.

karl
